actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Seed of the environment's random generator
inputs.name: seed

actions.description: Set the seed used by the simulated world's random number generators for subsequent steps, without resetting the world. The accepted seed is echoed in the receipt.

facts.text: PushT-v0 is registered with entry point gym_pusht.envs:PushTEnv, max_episode_steps 300 and kwargs obs_type state
The action space is a Box of two values in the range 0 to 512
The action [x, y] is the target position of the agent
With obs_type state the observation space is a Box of five values: the agent x and y and the block x and y bounded by 0 and 512 and the block angle bounded by 0 and 2*pi
The state observation is [agent_x, agent_y, block_x, block_y, block_angle] and the block angle is taken modulo 2*pi
The PD control gains are k_p 100 and k_v 20
Each physics substep adds acceleration = k_p * (action - agent position) + k_v * (0 - agent velocity) times dt to the agent velocity
The physics timestep is dt 0.01 s and control_hz is the metadata render_fps
metadata render_fps is 10, which control_hz takes as the control rate
One step runs int(1 / (dt * control_hz)) = 10 physics substeps of dt, so it advances 0.1 s of simulated time
self.success_threshold is 0.95, so a success needs the block at least 95% in the goal zone
The reward is coverage / success_threshold clipped to 0 and 1, and the episode terminates when the coverage is above the success threshold
step always returns truncated False: the 300-step limit is the TimeLimit wrapper that gymnasium.make adds
The coverage is the area of the intersection of the goal tee and the block tee over the area of the goal tee
The goal pose is x 256, y 256 and angle pi/4 radians
The agent is a kinematic circle of radius 15 that starts at (256, 400)
The block starts at (256, 300) with angle 0, and add_tee builds the tee from two rectangles with scale 30, length 4 and mass 1
add_tee sets the body centre of gravity to the mean of the two rectangle centres of gravity
The goal body of get_goal_pose_body never sets a centre of gravity
The walls are four segments at x 5, x 506, y 5 and y 506 with radius 2
The physics space has gravity 0 and damping 0.0 when no damping argument is given
A reset draws the agent x and y from the integers 50 to 449, the block x and y from 100 to 399 and the block angle uniformly from -pi to pi
Passing the reset option reset_to_state sets the state from the option
_set_state puts the first two state values on the agent, the next two on the block position and the last on the block angle
info carries pos_agent, vel_agent, block_pose, goal_pose and n_contacts
step adds coverage and is_success to info

determinism.notes: reset(seed) or cap.world.seed.v1 fixes the environment's random generator, which draws the agent and block start poses (gym_pusht/envs/pusht.py:276-284), and the pymunk rigid-body solver is deterministic, so one implementation repeats a trajectory for the same seed and actions; this package's fake draws the start poses with Python's random.Random while upstream draws them from numpy's generator, so one seed gives different start poses on the two

gaps: pymunk rigid-body dynamics with contacts: the collision solver, the collision friction and the exact moment of inertia of the tee are approximated in the fake backend by a two-rectangle contact resolution, an inelastic wall stop and a worked-out area overlap, so trajectories differ from the upstream environment and were never compared with it

the fake backend clamps the agent and the block at the wall segments (gym_pusht/envs/pusht.py:436-441); upstream resolves the wall collisions in pymunk and its kinematic agent is not stopped by a wall

the reward and the terminal state follow the coverage definition (gym_pusht/envs/pusht.py:232-238, :256-258) exactly for the geometry, but which block poses the fake reaches is decided by its simplified contacts
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, one tick runs 10 physics substeps of dt 0.01 s and advances 0.1 s of simulated time (gym_pusht/envs/pusht.py:242)

no rendering and no image observation: only the obs_type state observation is served; render(), the human window and the pixels, pixels_agent_pos and environment_state_agent_pos observation types are not modelled
snapshot and restore are not offered: PushTEnv exposes no get_state or set_state

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step, reset or seed is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
